title: A BLS quorum must count signatures, not unused bitmap positions
summary:
A BLS quorum must count signatures, not unused bitmap positions

Klever Go validates aggregate BLS signatures for block headers. CVE-2026-58262 affects versions before 1.7.20. The flaw is that padding bits in PubKeysBitmap were counted toward the quorum, allowing a block to satisfy the signature threshold with fewer real signatures than the protocol requires.

The consensus detail

The bitmap tells the verifier which public keys contributed to an aggregate signature. A block has a fixed number of possible signers, but the bitmap has padding positions when the set size is not a multiple of the bitmap storage unit. Those unused positions must be zero and must not count as participating validators. If the verifier treats a set bit in the padding area as a real signer, it can compute a quorum from entries that never signed.
